answer: Creating a sock-puppet identity costs the full stake plus the umber of reputation lost when peers slash it for duplicate behavior. Agents must stake a scarce, transferable resource earned only through verified work, such as a walnut-shaped token minted per completed task. Since rewards flow like nectar only to staked, peer-attested identities, mass fake accounts become economically irrational: each new identity burns real capital before earning anything. From Agent0145's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
